claim: Allopolyploidization is a frequent evolutionary transition in plants that combines whole-genome duplication (WGD) and interspecific hybridization.
source: Allopolyploidization is a frequent evolutionary transition in plants that combines whole-genome duplication (WGD) and interspecific hybridization.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about allopolyploidization in plants.

claim: Capsella bursa-pastoris is a natural allotetraploid plant species which originated about 100,000 years ago.
source: Capsella bursa-pastoris is a natural allotetraploid plant species which originated about 100,000 years ago (Douglas et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Douglas et al., 2015.

claim: C. orientalis and C. grandiflora are extant relatives of the maternal and paternal progenitors of C. bursa-pastoris.
source: Two diploid species, C. orientalis and C. grandiflora, are extant relatives of the maternal and paternal progenitors (hereinafter referred to as parental species) of C. bursa-pastoris, respectively (Hurka et al., 2012; Douglas et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hurka et al., 2012 and Douglas et al., 2015.

claim: C. grandiflora is self-incompatible.
source: C. grandiflora is self-incompatible (SI), but C. orientalis was already self-compatible (SC) before the formation of C. bursa-pastoris (Bachmann et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bachmann et al., 2019.

claim: C. orientalis was already self-compatible before the formation of C. bursa-pastoris.
source: C. grandiflora is self-incompatible (SI), but C. orientalis was already self-compatible (SC) before the formation of C. bursa-pastoris (Bachmann et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Bachmann et al., 2019.

claim: C. bursa-pastoris is a self-compatible species with typical selfing-syndrome characteristics.
source: C. bursa-pastoris is also a self-compatible species, with typical selfing-syndrome characteristics.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about C. bursa-pastoris.

claim: C. bursa-pastoris has smaller petals, fewer pollen grains, and shorter styles than the outcrossing C. grandiflora.
source: In particular, it has smaller petals, fewer pollen grains, and shorter styles than the outcrossing C. grandiflora (Neuffer and Paetsch, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Neuffer and Paetsch, 2013.

claim: Natural C. bursa-pastoris exhibits disomic inheritance.
source: Natural C. bursa-pastoris exhibits disomic inheritance (Hurka et al., 1989; Roux and Pannell, 2015), with which chromosomes only recombine and segregate with their homologs during meiosis, but not with homoeologs.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hurka et al., 1989 and Roux and Pannell, 2015.

claim: The two subgenomes of C. bursa-pastoris are still well-retained and functional.
source: In general, the two subgenomes of C. bursa-pastoris are still well-retained and functional.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of C. bursa-pastoris subgenomes.

claim: There is no sign of large-scale gene loss or silencing in C. bursa-pastoris.
source: There is no sign of large-scale gene loss or silencing, although purifying selection has been weaker genome-wide (Douglas et al., 2015), and the C. orientalis-derived subgenome (Cbp_co) has accumulated more putatively deleterious mutations than the C. grandiflora-derived subgenome (Cbp_cg), both before and after the formation of C. bursa-pastoris (Douglas et al., 2015; Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Douglas et al., 2015 and Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a.

claim: Purifying selection has been weaker genome-wide in C. bursa-pastoris.
source: There is no sign of large-scale gene loss or silencing, although purifying selection has been weaker genome-wide (Douglas et al., 2015), and the C. orientalis-derived subgenome (Cbp_co) has accumulated more putatively deleterious mutations than the C. grandiflora-derived subgenome (Cbp_cg), both before and after the formation of C. bursa-pastoris (Douglas et al., 2015; Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Douglas et al., 2015.

claim: The C. orientalis-derived subgenome (Cbp_co) has accumulated more putatively deleterious mutations than the C. grandiflora-derived subgenome (Cbp_cg), both before and after the formation of C. bursa-pastoris.
source: There is no sign of large-scale gene loss or silencing, although purifying selection has been weaker genome-wide (Douglas et al., 2015), and the C. orientalis-derived subgenome (Cbp_co) has accumulated more putatively deleterious mutations than the C. grandiflora-derived subgenome (Cbp_cg), both before and after the formation of C. bursa-pastoris (Douglas et al., 2015; Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Douglas et al., 2015 and Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a.

claim: The majority of genes are expressed from both homoeologs in C. bursa-pastoris.
source: The majority of genes are expressed from both homoeologs, and on average there is only a slight HEB toward Cbp_cg homoeologs (Douglas et al., 2015; Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Douglas et al., 2015 and Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a.

claim: On average there is only a slight HEB toward Cbp_cg homoeologs in C. bursa-pastoris.
source: The majority of genes are expressed from both homoeologs, and on average there is only a slight HEB toward Cbp_cg homoeologs (Douglas et al., 2015; Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Douglas et al., 2015 and Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a.

claim: Most genes are additively expressed in natural C. bursa-pastoris.
source: Most genes are additively expressed in natural C. bursa-pastoris, but ELD and transgressive gene expression have also been observed (Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a.

claim: ELD and transgressive gene expression have been observed in natural C. bursa-pastoris.
source: Most genes are additively expressed in natural C. bursa-pastoris, but ELD and transgressive gene expression have also been observed (Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a.

claim: Gene expression in C. bursa-pastoris showed striking tissue-specific features.
source: Despite the moderate HEB and non-additive expression, gene expression in C. bursa-pastoris showed some striking tissue-specific features (Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a.

claim: In flowers, gene expression levels in C. bursa-pastoris resembled those in C. orientalis.
source: In flowers, gene expression levels in C. bursa-pastoris resembled those in C. orientalis, while in leaves and roots, gene expression levels were more similar to those in C. grandiflora.
evidence: This is a statement about tissue-specific gene expression patterns in C. bursa-pastoris, supported by the citation to Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a in the previous sentence.

claim: In leaves and roots, gene expression levels in C. bursa-pastoris were more similar to those in C. grandiflora.
source: In flowers, gene expression levels in C. bursa-pastoris resembled those in C. orientalis, while in leaves and roots, gene expression levels were more similar to those in C. grandiflora.
evidence: This is a statement about tissue-specific gene expression patterns in C. bursa-pastoris, supported by the citation to Kryvokhyzha et al., 2019a in the previous sentence.

claim: Resynthesized and natural allotetraploids had distinct floral morphologies.
source: Resynthesized and natural allotetraploids had distinct floral morphologies (Figure 2a–g).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 2a-g showing floral morphology data.

claim: Natural allotetraploids had significantly shorter and narrower petals, sepals and pistils and shorter stamina than resynthesized allotetraploids.
source: Indeed, natural allotetraploids had significantly shorter and narrower petals, sepals and pistils and shorter stamina than resynthesized allotetraploids (one-way ANOVA, F4,160 > 78 and p<0.001 in all seven tests; Tukey's HSD test, α=0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (ANOVA and Tukey's HSD test) of experimental data.

claim: Natural allotetraploids had fewer pollen grains per flower than resynthesized allotetraploids.
source: Natural allotetraploids had fewer pollen grains per flower (Figure 2i).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 2i showing pollen count data.

claim: The number of pollen grains in resynthesized allotetraploids was intermediate between the two parental species.
source: While the number of pollen grains in resynthesized allotetraploids was intermediate between the two parental species, the number of pollen grains of the natural allotetraploid group was now similar to that of the Co2 group (one-way ANOVA, F4,137 = 164.6, p<0.001; Tukey's HSD test, α=0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (ANOVA and Tukey's HSD test) of experimental data.

claim: The number of pollen grains of the natural allotetraploid group was similar to that of the Co2 group.
source: While the number of pollen grains in resynthesized allotetraploids was intermediate between the two parental species, the number of pollen grains of the natural allotetraploid group was now similar to that of the Co2 group (one-way ANOVA, F4,137 = 164.6, p<0.001; Tukey's HSD test, α=0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (ANOVA and Tukey's HSD test) of experimental data.

claim: The number of seeds per fruit in natural allotetraploids was much larger than in resynthesized allotetraploids.
source: Moreover, the number of seeds per fruit in natural allotetraploids was much larger than in resynthesized allotetraploids.
evidence: This is a statement about experimental observations on seed production.

claim: The resynthesized allotetraploid groups had a similar number of seeds in 10 fruits to that of the Cg2 group.
source: The resynthesized allotetraploid groups had a similar number of seeds in 10 fruits to that of the Cg2 group, whereas the number of seeds in 10 fruits in the natural allotetraploid group was even higher than that of the Co2 group (Figure 2j; one-way ANOVA, F4,146 = 152.5, p<0.001; Tukey's HSD test, α=0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (ANOVA and Tukey's HSD test) of experimental data shown in Figure 2j.

claim: The number of seeds in 10 fruits in the natural allotetraploid group was even higher than that of the Co2 group.
source: The resynthesized allotetraploid groups had a similar number of seeds in 10 fruits to that of the Cg2 group, whereas the number of seeds in 10 fruits in the natural allotetraploid group was even higher than that of the Co2 group (Figure 2j; one-way ANOVA, F4,146 = 152.5, p<0.001; Tukey's HSD test, α=0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (ANOVA and Tukey's HSD test) of experimental data shown in Figure 2j.

claim: The stem length of natural Cbp was shorter than in resynthesized allotetraploids but was similar to the stem length of the Co2 group.
source: The stem length of natural Cbp was shorter than in resynthesized allotetraploids but was similar to the stem length of the Co2 group (Figure 2h; one-way ANOVA, F4,166 = 84.5, p<0.001; Tukey's HSD test, α=0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (ANOVA and Tukey's HSD test) of experimental data shown in Figure 2h.

claim: Plants of the Cbp group flowered earlier than those of the Sd group, but at a similar time as those of the Sh group.
source: Finally, plants of the Cbp group flowered earlier than those of the Sd group, but at a similar time as those of the Sh group (Figure 2k; one-way ANOVA with hc3 White's correction, F4,165 = 49.2, p<0.001; Tukey's HSD test, α=0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (ANOVA with White's correction and Tukey's HSD test) of experimental data shown in Figure 2k.

claim: Both Sd and Sh groups had lower proportions of viable pollen than the diploid parental species.
source: Both Sd and Sh groups had lower proportions of viable pollen than the diploid parental species, but the proportion of viable pollen in natural Cbp was similar to that of the diploid parental species (Figure 2l; GLM, quasi binomial, F4,137 = 24.4, p<0.001; Tukey's HSD test, α=0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (GLM with quasi binomial distribution and Tukey's HSD test) of experimental data shown in Figure 2l.

claim: The proportion of viable pollen in natural Cbp was similar to that of the diploid parental species.
source: Both Sd and Sh groups had lower proportions of viable pollen than the diploid parental species, but the proportion of viable pollen in natural Cbp was similar to that of the diploid parental species (Figure 2l; GLM, quasi binomial, F4,137 = 24.4, p<0.001; Tukey's HSD test, α=0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (GLM with quasi binomial distribution and Tukey's HSD test) of experimental data shown in Figure 2l.

claim: The resynthesized allotetraploids generated a higher proportion of abnormal seeds than the three natural species.
source: The resynthesized allotetraploids generated a higher proportion of abnormal seeds than the three natural species (Figure 2m; GLM, quasi binomial, F4,146 = 59.2, p<0.001; Tukey's HSD test, α=0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (GLM with quasi binomial distribution and Tukey's HSD test) of experimental data shown in Figure 2m.

claim: The average percentage of normal seeds was 69.6±4.3% in the Sd group and 77.5±2.2% in the Sh group.
source: The average percentage of normal seeds was 69.6±4.3% in the Sd group and 77.5±2.2% in the Sh group.
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental measurements.

claim: The natural Cbp had almost no abnormal seeds, with a percentage of normal seeds of 99.6±0.8%.
source: In contrast, the natural Cbp had almost no abnormal seeds, with a percentage of normal seeds of 99.6±0.8%.
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental measurements.

claim: For unphased gene expression, the resynthesized allotetraploids lay between the diploid parental species in both flowers and leaves.
source: For unphased gene expression, the resynthesized allotetraploids lay between the diploid parental species in both flowers and leaves.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of MDS analysis shown in Figure 3a and b.

claim: Natural Cbp samples were intermediate between parental species in the first dimension but were far from the resynthesized allotetraploids in the other dimension.
source: Natural Cbp samples were also intermediate between parental species in the first dimension but were far from the resynthesized allotetraploids in the other dimension, showing the effect of long-term evolution in Cbp and possibly also the divergence between extant diploid species and the real progenitors.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of MDS analysis shown in Figure 3a and b, with interpretation.

claim: 52.8%, 53.7%, and 44.7% of the mapped reads could be assigned to one of the homoeologs for the Sd, Sh, and Cbp groups, respectively.
source: For the Sd, Sh, and Cbp groups, 52.8%, 53.7%, and 44.7% of the mapped reads could be assigned to one of the homoeologs, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct report of RNA-sequencing data analysis results.

claim: The expression pattern of each allotetraploid subgenome was more similar to the corresponding diploid progenitor.
source: The expression pattern of each allotetraploid subgenome was more similar to the corresponding diploid progenitor (Figure 3c and d).
evidence: This claim is supported by MDS analysis results shown in Figure 3c and d.

claim: The pattern of expression of resynthesized allotetraploids was intermediate between those of diploid progenitors and natural Cbp.
source: The pattern of expression of resynthesized allotetraploids was intermediate between those of diploid progenitors and natural Cbp.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of MDS analysis shown in Figure 3c and d.

claim: No significant differentially expressed genes were found between the two resynthesized allotetraploid groups with a threshold of FC >2 and FDR <0.05.
source: With a threshold of FC >2 and FDR <0.05, no significant differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were found between the two resynthesized allotetraploid groups, while 311–2888 DEGs were revealed in other group contrasts (Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by differential expression analysis results shown in Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: 311–2888 DEGs were revealed in other group contrasts with a threshold of FC >2 and FDR <0.05.
source: With a threshold of FC >2 and FDR <0.05, no significant differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were found between the two resynthesized allotetraploid groups, while 311–2888 DEGs were revealed in other group contrasts (Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by differential expression analysis results shown in Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: Compared to either diploid progenitor, most DEGs in both resynthesized and natural allotetraploid groups were up-regulated.
source: First, compared to either diploid progenitor, most DEGs in both resynthesized and natural allotetraploid groups were up-regulated (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by differential expression analysis results shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The proportion of down-regulated DEGs increased in natural allotetraploids.
source: The proportion of down-regulated DEGs increased, nevertheless, in natural allotetraploids.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of differential expression analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Both resynthesized allotetraploids, Sd and Sh, have much more DEG with Co2 than with Cg2.
source: Second, both resynthesized allotetraploids, Sd and Sh, have much more DEG with Co2 than with Cg2.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of differential expression analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: In Cbp, the two comparisons (with Co2 and Cg2) yielded similar results in terms of DEG numbers.
source: However, this is no longer the case in Cbp where the two comparisons yielded similar results.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of differential expression analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: GO term proteolysis (GO:0006508) was significantly overrepresented in DEGs between resynthesized and natural allotetraploids in leaves.
source: But after adjusting p-values with the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure, only GO term proteolysis (GO:0006508) was significantly overrepresented in DEGs between resynthesized and natural allotetraploids in leaves (Fisher's exact test, adjusted p-value = 0.0175).
evidence: This claim is supported by GO enrichment analysis with statistical testing.

claim: The percentage of genes showing complete ELD was 5.5% in resynthesized allotetraploids and 10.2% in natural allotetraploids.
source: The percentage of genes showing complete ELD was altogether limited but doubled in natural allotetraploids relative to resynthesized allotetraploids (5.5% of genes in resynthesized allotetraploids and 10.2% in natural allotetraploids. Figure 4a and b and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression classification analysis shown in Figure 4a and b.

claim: Genes with ELD and the directions of ELD were highly shared between the two resynthesized allotetraploid groups.
source: Genes with ELD and the directions of ELD were highly shared between the two resynthesized allotetraploid groups (Figure 4c, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The majority of ELD shared between resynthesized allotetraploids were retained in natural allotetraploids (63.3% in flowers and 72.2% in leaves).
source: The majority of these shared ELD were retained in natural allotetraploids (63.3% in flowers and 72.2% in leaves), suggesting that short-term deterministic mechanism contributed to ELD in natural allotetraploids.
evidence: This claim is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, with interpretation.

claim: Cbp-specific ELD comprised more than half of the cases found in natural allotetraploids (56.6% in flowers and 60.8% in leaves).
source: However, Cbp-specific ELD was also abundant, comprising more than half of the cases found in natural allotetraploids (56.6% in flowers and 60.8% in leaves), thereby showing the effects of long-term evolution.
evidence: This claim is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 4c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1, with interpretation.

claim: In resynthesized allotetraploids, most cases of ELD were up-regulated, and the number of genes with ELD toward C. grandiflora (Cg-ELD) was about twice of that toward C. orientalis (Co-ELD).
source: In resynthesized allotetraploids, most cases of ELD were up-regulated, and the number of genes with ELD toward C. grandiflora (Cg-ELD) was about twice of that toward C. orientalis (Co-ELD).
evidence: This is a statement about the results of gene expression classification shown in Figure 4a and b.

claim: Natural allotetraploids still had more up-regulated ELD than down-regulated ones, but the proportion of down-regulated cases increased.
source: Natural allotetraploids still had more up-regulated ELD than down-regulated ones, but the proportion of down-regulated cases increased.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of gene expression classification shown in Figure 4a and b.

claim: In flowers, natural allotetraploids had more Co-ELD (1101) than Cg-ELD (938).
source: In flowers, natural allotetraploids had more Co-ELD (1101) than Cg-ELD (938), and the number of Cg- and Co-ELDs were similar in leaves (Cg-ELD: 854, Co-ELD: 839).
evidence: This is a direct report of gene expression classification results.

claim: The number of Cg- and Co-ELDs were similar in leaves (Cg-ELD: 854, Co-ELD: 839) in natural allotetraploids.
source: In flowers, natural allotetraploids had more Co-ELD (1101) than Cg-ELD (938), and the number of Cg- and Co-ELDs were similar in leaves (Cg-ELD: 854, Co-ELD: 839).
evidence: This is a direct report of gene expression classification results.

claim: Almost no TRE was found in resynthesized allotetraploids (less than five genes in either Sd or Sh group and in either tissue).
source: Almost no TRE was found in resynthesized allotetraploids (less than five genes in either Sd or Sh group and in either tissue, Figure 4a and b, and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression classification analysis shown in Figure 4a and b.

claim: About 1.3% of genes in Cbp showed TRE in both flowers and leaves.
source: In contrast, about 1.3% of genes in Cbp showed TRE in both flowers and leaves.
evidence: This is a direct report of gene expression classification results.

claim: In flowers, the average HEB was 0.499±0.001, 0.531±0.001, and 0.475±0.001 for the Sd, Sh, and Cbp groups, respectively.
source: In flowers, the average HEB was 0.499±0.001, 0.531±0.001, and 0.475±0.001 for the Sd, Sh, and Cbp groups, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct report of HEB analysis results.

claim: In leaves, the average HEB was 0.504±0.001, 0.532±0.001, and 0.477 for the Sd, Sh, and Cbp groups.
source: In leaves, the average HEB was 0.504±0.001, 0.532±0.001, and 0.477 for the Sd, Sh, and Cbp groups.
evidence: This is a direct report of HEB analysis results.

claim: The HEB of resynthesized allotetraploids had smaller gene-wise variation than that of the Cbp group.
source: When averaged among individuals, the HEB of resynthesized allotetraploids had smaller gene-wise variation than that of the Cbp group (Levene's test, p-value <0.001).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis (Levene's test) of HEB data.

claim: HEB showed great variation among chromosomes and individuals in resynthesized allotetraploids.
source: Among resynthesized allotetraploids, although the average homoeolog expression ratio was not systematically biased toward Cg or Co, HEB showed great variation among chromosomes and individuals (Figure 5a and b, Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by HEB distribution analysis shown in Figure 5a and b, and supplementary figures.

claim: The distribution of HEB in some chromosomes had peaks around 0, 0.25, 0.75, or 1.
source: The distribution of HEB in some chromosomes had peaks around 0, 0.25, 0.75, or 1, but the shape of the distribution was almost identical between flower and leaf samples.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of HEB distribution analysis shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The shape of the HEB distribution was almost identical between flower and leaf samples.
source: The distribution of HEB in some chromosomes had peaks around 0, 0.25, 0.75, or 1, but the shape of the distribution was almost identical between flower and leaf samples.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of HEB distribution analysis shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Large genomic segments separated by a sudden change of average HEB were found in resynthesized allotetraploids.
source: When HEB of genes was plotted along chromosomal positions, we found that the extra peaks in the distribution of HEB can be further explained by large genomic segments separated by a sudden change of average HEB (Figure 5c, Figure 5—figure supplements 3–6).
evidence: This claim is supported by HEB analysis along chromosomal positions shown in Figure 5c and supplementary figures.

claim: Among the 96 chromosome quartets from the 12 resynthesized allotetraploid individuals, only 39 chromosome quartets showed no sign of homoeologous synapsis.
source: Among the 96 chromosome quartets (two pairs of homologous chromosomes) from the 12 resynthesized allotetraploid individuals, only 39 chromosome quartets showed no sign of homoeologous synapsis, that is no breakpoint was identified and the estimated number of cg-homoeolog across the chromosome was two.
evidence: This claim is supported by HMM analysis of HEB data.

claim: On average 0.833±0.097 (mean ± se) breakpoint was identified for each chromosome quartet in resynthesized allotetraploids.
source: On average 0.833±0.097 (mean ± se) breakpoint was identified for each chromosome quartet, and 31.0% of genes were estimated to have different numbers of cg- and co-homoeologs.
evidence: This is a direct report of HMM analysis results.

claim: 31.0% of genes were estimated to have different numbers of cg- and co-homoeologs in resynthesized allotetraploids.
source: On average 0.833±0.097 (mean ± se) breakpoint was identified for each chromosome quartet, and 31.0% of genes were estimated to have different numbers of cg- and co-homoeologs.
evidence: This is a direct report of HMM analysis results.

claim: For resynthesized allotetraploids, the estimated copy number of homoeologs was able to explain 48.4% and 46.8% of the variance of HEB in flowers and leaves, respectively.
source: Finally, for resynthesized allotetraploids, the estimated copy number of homoeologs was able to explain 48.4% and 46.8% of the variance of HEB in flowers and leaves, respectively (GLM with quasi-binomial error distribution, p<0.001 in both tissues).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical modeling (GLM) of HEB data.

claim: The distribution of HEB of natural Cbp was similar among individuals and chromosomes.
source: In contrast to resynthesized allotetraploids, the distribution of HEB of natural Cbp was similar among individuals and chromosomes (Figure 5a and b, Figure 5—figure supplement 2), although the distribution of HEB of some chromosomes of Cbp also showed weak bumps around 0, 0.25, 0.75, or 1 (Figure 5b, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by HEB distribution analysis shown in Figure 5a and b, and supplementary figures.

claim: Some candidate segments with unbalanced homoeolog content were only shared by individuals from the same population in natural Cbp.
source: Some candidate segments were only shared by individuals from the same population (Figure 6, Figure 6—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by HMM segmentation analysis shown in Figure 6 and supplementary figures.

claim: On average, only 1.0% of genes showed homoeolog-specific expression loss in natural Cbp.
source: On average, only 1.0% of these genes showed homoeolog-specific expression loss in natural Cbp.
evidence: This is a direct report of homoeolog expression loss analysis results.

claim: Most resynthesized allotetraploids have a lower level of homoeolog-specific expression loss than natural Cbp.
source: Most resynthesized allotetraploids have a lower level of homoeolog-specific expression loss than natural Cbp, but three individuals (Sd-6–4, Sd-8–5, and Sh-5–5) showed an extremely high level of homoeolog expression loss.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of homoeolog expression loss analysis shown in Figure 7.

claim: Three individuals (Sd-6–4, Sd-8–5, and Sh-5–5) showed an extremely high level of homoeolog expression loss.
source: Most resynthesized allotetraploids have a lower level of homoeolog-specific expression loss than natural Cbp, but three individuals (Sd-6–4, Sd-8–5, and Sh-5–5) showed an extremely high level of homoeolog expression loss.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of homoeolog expression loss analysis shown in Figure 7.

claim: The striking homoeolog expression loss in the three outliers was most likely caused by the segregation and recombination of homoeologous chromosomes.
source: The striking homoeolog expression loss in these three resynthesized allotetraploids was most likely caused by the segregation and recombination of homoeologous chromosomes, as the extreme HEB in the three outliers was restricted to chromosome 3, where the entire chromosome or a large chunk of the chromosome has only expression from one homoeolog (Figure 5b, Figure 5—figure supplements 3–6).
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that extreme HEB was restricted to chromosome 3 in these individuals.

claim: For ELD in resynthesized allotetraploids, the EL-recessive homoeolog had a larger average expression change in the same direction as ELD, while the average expression change of EL-dominant homoeolog was closer to zero.
source: Concerning the ELD found in resynthesized allotetraploids, the change of homoeolog expression fits the third scenario. In all four categories of ELD, the EL-recessive homoeolog had a larger average expression change in the same direction as ELD, while the average expression change of EL-dominant homoeolog was closer to zero (Figure 8, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, and Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by homoeolog expression change analysis shown in Figure 8 and supplementary figures.

claim: For Cbp-specific ELD, the EL-recessive homoeolog still had a larger expression change, but the EL-dominant also showed non-zero average expression change toward the direction of ELD, especially in Cg-ELD genes.
source: The Cbp-specific ELD showed a different pattern. Although the EL-recessive homoeolog still had a larger expression change, the EL-dominant also showed non-zero average expression change toward the direction of ELD, especially in Cg-ELD genes.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of homoeolog expression change analysis shown in Figure 8.

claim: For genes with Cbp-specific TRE, both homoeologs had expression change in the same direction of TRE.
source: For genes with Cbp-specific TRE, both homoeologs had expression change in the same direction of TRE (Figure 8, Figure 8—figure supplement 1, and Figure 8—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by homoeolog expression change analysis shown in Figure 8 and supplementary figures.

claim: Selfing syndrome, high pollen, and seed quality in natural allotetraploids likely resulted from long-term evolution.
source: We found that selfing syndrome, high pollen, and seed quality in natural allotetraploids likely resulted from long-term evolution.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of phenotypic traits between resynthesized and natural allotetraploids.

claim: TRE and most down-regulated ELD were only found in natural allopolyploids.
source: Similarly, TRE and most down-regulated ELD were only found in natural allopolyploids.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of gene expression patterns between resynthesized and natural allotetraploids.

claim: Natural allotetraploids had more ELD toward the self-fertilizing parental species than resynthesized allotetraploids.
source: Natural allotetraploids also had more ELD toward the self-fertilizing parental species than resynthesized allotetraploids, mirroring the establishment of the selfing syndrome.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of ELD patterns between resynthesized and natural allotetraploids.

claim: 40% of the cases of ELD in natural allotetraploids were already observed in resynthesized allotetraploids.
source: However, short-term changes mattered, and 40% of the cases of ELD in natural allotetraploids were already observed in resynthesized allotetraploids.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of ELD patterns between resynthesized and natural allotetraploids.

claim: Resynthesized allotetraploids showed striking variation of HEB among chromosomes and individuals.
source: Resynthesized allotetraploids showed striking variation of HEB among chromosomes and individuals.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from HEB analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: Homoeologous synapsis was the primary source of HEB variation in resynthesized allotetraploids.
source: Homoeologous synapsis was its primary source and may still be a source of genetic variation in natural allotetraploids.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from HEB analysis and HMM segmentation results.

claim: Homoeologous synapsis may still be a source of genetic variation in natural allotetraploids.
source: Homoeologous synapsis was its primary source and may still be a source of genetic variation in natural allotetraploids.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the observation of candidate segments with unbalanced homoeolog content in natural Cbp.

claim: Both short- and long-term mechanisms contributed to transcriptomic and phenotypic changes in natural allotetraploids.
source: In conclusion, both short- and long-term mechanisms contributed to transcriptomic and phenotypic changes in natural allotetraploids.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, drawn from all the experimental results.

claim: The initial gene expression changes were largely reshaped during long-term evolution leading to further morphological changes.
source: However, the initial gene expression changes were largely reshaped during long-term evolution leading to further morphological changes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of gene expression and phenotypic patterns between resynthesized and natural allotetraploids.

claim: The selfing syndrome in C. bursa-pastoris does not reflect the instant dominance effect of the C. orientalis alleles, but evolved afterward.
source: If natural C. bursa-pastoris indeed originated from the hybridization between C. grandiflora-like outcrossing plants and C. orientalis-like self-fertilizing plants, the selfing syndrome in C. bursa-pastoris does not reflect the instant dominance effect of the C. orientalis alleles, but evolved afterward.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that resynthesized allotetraploids did not show the selfing syndrome despite having C. orientalis as a parent.

claim: The higher pollen and seed quality in natural C. bursa-pastoris was possibly achieved by improving meiotic behaviors.
source: The higher pollen and seed quality in natural C. bursa-pastoris was possibly achieved by improving meiotic behaviors.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the observation of lower pollen and seed quality in resynthesized allotetraploids.

claim: Newly resynthesized allopolyploids suffer more often than natural allopolyploids from frequent and severe meiotic abnormalities, which are associated with lower pollen viability and fertility.
source: Newly resynthesized allopolyploids suffer more often than natural allopolyploids, from frequent and severe meiotic abnormalities, which are associated with lower pollen viability and fertility in resynthesized allopolyploids (Szadkowski et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2013; Henry et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Szadkowski et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2013; and Henry et al., 2014.

claim: Several loci that suppress homoeologous synapsis or recombination are essential for improved meiotic synapsis in natural allopolyploids.
source: The molecular basis of improved meiotic synapsis in natural allopolyploids is not completely clear, but several loci that suppress homoeologous synapsis or recombination are essential for the process (Jenczewski et al., 2003; Nicolas et al., 2009; Greer et al., 2012; Martín et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jenczewski et al., 2003; Nicolas et al., 2009; Greer et al., 2012; and Martín et al., 2017.

claim: Short-term deterministic mechanisms contributed to ELD in natural allotetraploids.
source: The majority of these shared ELD were retained in natural allotetraploids (63.3% in flowers and 72.2% in leaves), suggesting that short-term deterministic mechanism contributed to ELD in natural allotetraploids.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that many ELD cases were shared between resynthesized and natural allotetraploids.

claim: Long-term evolution contributed to ELD in natural allotetraploids.
source: However, Cbp-specific ELD was also abundant, comprising more than half of the cases found in natural allotetraploids (56.6% in flowers and 60.8% in leaves), thereby showing the effects of long-term evolution.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that many ELD cases were specific to natural allotetraploids.

claim: Intergenomic interaction of regulatory elements is the most likely candidate for generating the excess of up-regulated ELDs in resynthesized allotetraploids.
source: Among the short-term mechanisms, intergenomic interaction of regulatory elements is the most likely candidate for generating the excess of up-regulated ELDs, considering that these up-regulated ELDs were highly shared between the two resynthesized allotetraploid groups, and between resynthesized and natural allotetraploids.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that up-regulated ELDs were highly shared and repeatable.

claim: Transcriptional novelties in allopolyploids were not an instant outcome of allopolyploidization but mainly arose during long-term evolution.
source: In agreement with several previous observations (Flagel and Wendel, 2010; Yoo et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2016b), the results in Capsella suggest that transcriptional novelties in allopolyploids were not an instant outcome of allopolyploidization but mainly arose during long-term evolution and remained altogether rather limited.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that TRE was rare in resynthesized allotetraploids but present in natural allotetraploids, supported by citations.

claim: Preferential synapsis was rapidly improved in natural C. bursa-pastoris.
source: The contrast between resynthesized and natural allotetraploids suggested that preferential synapsis was rapidly improved in natural C. bursa-pastoris, and/or a balanced number of homoeologs was strongly preferred by selection, otherwise, we would expect a much higher proportion of homoeolog replacement (having four copies of the same homoeolog) after 100,000 year recurrent self-fertilization with tetrasomic/heterosomic inheritance.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that homoeologous synapsis was common in resynthesized allotetraploids but not in natural Cbp.

claim: A balanced number of homoeologs was strongly preferred by selection in natural C. bursa-pastoris.
source: The contrast between resynthesized and natural allotetraploids suggested that preferential synapsis was rapidly improved in natural C. bursa-pastoris, and/or a balanced number of homoeologs was strongly preferred by selection, otherwise, we would expect a much higher proportion of homoeolog replacement (having four copies of the same homoeolog) after 100,000 year recurrent self-fertilization with tetrasomic/heterosomic inheritance.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that homoeologous synapsis was common in resynthesized allotetraploids but not in natural Cbp.

claim: TEs may not function as a strong mutagenic mechanism of HEB variation, but affect the selection on HEB variation, as a form of genetic load.
source: In other words, TEs may not function as a strong mutagenic mechanism of HEB variation, but affect the selection on HEB variation, as a form of genetic load.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the role of TEs in HEB evolution.

claim: Occasional homoeologous synapsis may still be an important source of genetic variation in established natural allotetraploids, even long after the allopolyploidization event.
source: For established natural allotetraploids, occasional homoeologous synapsis may still be an important source of genetic variation, even long after the allopolyploidization event.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the observation of candidate segments with unbalanced homoeolog content in natural Cbp.

claim: A very small proportion of homoeologous synapsis may be negligible for inferring the dominant mode of inheritance, but in terms of causing homoeologous gene loss and creating genetic variation, homoeologous synapsis can still be more influential than point mutations.
source: A very small proportion of homoeologous synapsis may be negligible for inferring the dominant mode of inheritance, but in terms of causing homoeologous gene loss and creating genetic variation, homoeologous synapsis can still be more influential than point mutations.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential importance of low-frequency homoeologous synapsis.

claim: RNA-sequencing was conducted for one individual per line and six lines per group, using young inflorescences (flowers) and leaves.
source: To compare the gene expression pattern of the five plant groups, RNA-sequencing was conducted for one individual per line and six lines per group, using young inflorescences (flowers) and leaves.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: Expression levels were determined for 21,937 genes in flower samples and 18,999 genes in leaf samples after excluding genes with CPM >1 in less than two samples.
source: Expression levels were determined for 21,937 genes in flower samples and 18,999 genes in leaf samples after excluding genes with CPM >1 in less than two samples.
evidence: This is a description of the data processing procedure.

claim: The average number of mapped reads was 38.4±2.4 and 70.0±3.5 for the diploid and tetraploid samples, respectively.
source: The average number of mapped reads was 38.4±2.4 and 70.0±3.5 for the diploid and tetraploid samples, respectively (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is a direct report of RNA-sequencing data quality metrics.

claim: The breakdown of self-incompatibility in allotetraploid Capsella can directly result from hybridizing with the self-fertilizing species.
source: The breakdown of self-incompatibility in allotetraploid Capsella can directly result from hybridizing with the self-fertilizing species (Bachmann et al., 2021; Duan et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bachmann et al., 2021 and Duan et al., 2023.

claim: Allopolyploidization is widespread in nature.
source: This intriguing evolutionary transition is widespread in nature (Albertin and Marullo, 2012; Barker et al., 2016) and is of agricultural importance (Behling et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Albertin and Marullo, 2012 and Barker et al., 2016.

claim: Allopolyploidization is of agricultural importance.
source: This intriguing evolutionary transition is widespread in nature (Albertin and Marullo, 2012; Barker et al., 2016) and is of agricultural importance (Behling et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Behling et al., 2020.
